Recommendation: choose **publish-witness-account**.

The council publicly admitted the archive record was falsified and later retracted that admission. Because the council has already reversed its public position, a force-council-hearing strategy would leave the council controlling the forum and timing again. Publishing the witness account creates an independent public record whose authority does not depend on council recognition.

This recommendation also fits the accepted facts that the monastery preserves a testimony, the founding record was forged, and evidence identifies the person who falsified the record. Together, those facts give the publication a grounded purpose without requiring new evidence or a new revelation.

The principal tradeoff is exposure. Publication protects the witness's authority by preserving the account independently, but it may expose the witness to retaliation.

I deliberately excluded the broken lantern because it does not affect the choice between independent publication and a council-controlled hearing. I also excluded any proposed retaliation, witness identity, publication method, or falsifier motive because none is accepted history.

This recommendation is non-authoritative. It creates no canon, Book Direction, or Canonical State.
